title: Gender & Definite Articles
subtitle: Decode masculine, feminine, neuter, and plural nouns using visual endings and color patterns.

cheatSheet.summary: Every German noun has one of three grammatical genders—Masculine (der), Feminine (die), or Neuter (das)—plus Plural (die). Learn every noun with its article and color tag.
keyTakeaways: Masculine [M] (der): days, months, seasons, weather, and nouns ending in -er, -ismus, -ling.
Feminine [F] (die): nouns ending in -ung, -heit, -keit, -schaft, -tät, -ion, and ~90% of -e nouns.
Neuter [N] (das): all diminutives in -chen and -lein (even das Mädchen!), plus -ment, -um, and nominalized verbs.
Plural [PL] (die): ALL plural nouns take 'die' in the Nominative regardless of their singular gender.
cheatSheet.watchOut: Gender is grammatical, not biological! 'Das Mädchen' (the girl) is Neuter [N] solely because the diminutive ending '-chen' ALWAYS forces Neuter.

exercises.english: The newspaper is lying on the table.
exercises.fullGerman: Die Zeitung liegt auf dem Tisch.

nouns.caseTrigger: Subject of the sentence (Nominative) + '-ung' suffix is always Feminine [F]

exercises.rulePill: Nouns ending in '-ung' (Zeitung, Wohnung, Übung) are 100% Feminine [F] → Nominative takes 'die'.

nouns.caseTrigger: Subject of the sentence + '-chen' diminutive is always Neuter [N]

exercises.rulePill: Every diminutive ending in '-chen' or '-lein' is strictly Neuter [N] → 'das Mädchen' (never 'die').
'Kaffee' is Masculine [M] (like most hot drinks: der Tee, der Kakao) → Nominative takes 'der'.

exercises.english: The books are standing on the shelf.

nouns.caseTrigger: Plural subject → ALL plurals use 'die' in Nominative

exercises.rulePill: Singular 'das Buch' [N] becomes Plural 'die Bücher' [PL] → all plural nouns use 'die' in Nominative.

nouns.caseTrigger: Subject of 'stehen' — Feminine [F] noun ending in '-e'

exercises.rulePill: 'Lampe' is Feminine [F] ('die Lampe') → the Nominative indefinite article adds '-e': 'eine'.

exercises.promptHint: One article has the wrong gender. Click it and select the fix.
exercises.english: The bread roll is still quite warm.
exercises.fullGerman: Das Brötchen ist noch ganz warm.
exercises.rulePill: 'Brötchen' ends in '-chen' (singular because of 'ist') → diminutives are always Neuter [N]: 'Das Brötchen'.

nouns.caseTrigger: Nouns ending in '-heit' are always Feminine [F]

exercises.rulePill: Every noun ending in '-heit' or '-keit' (Freiheit, Gesundheit, Möglichkeit) is 100% Feminine [F] → 'die'.

exercises.instruction: Build a clean Nominative statement (keep the verb in Position 2).
exercises.rulePill: Nouns ending in '-um' (das Museum, das Zentrum) are Neuter [N], and the finite verb 'ist' sits in Position 2.

exercises.subject: wir
exercises.english: We are new students from Munich.
exercises.fullGerman: Wir sind neue Studenten aus München.
exercises.rulePill: 'sein' is irregular: ich bin, du bist, er/sie/es ist, wir sind, ihr seid, sie/Sie sind.
